chapter: Erroll Garner, the 1952 arrest and Florida
title: The 1952 heroin arrest and loss of his cabaret card
summary: Arrested for possession, he lost his New York cabaret card and income.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: You were arrested in 1952 for what?

I was sniffing then, yes. And I was drinking whiskey and smoking marijuana and everything else, and I didn't have time to find out if I had a habit of anything, you know, because I was using some of everything. But as soon as I dwindled down to just this one thing, the white horse that they say you mount and ride straight to hell, I got on that white horse, and he took me to hell. But I came back.
When did you first start using?
Well, after they took my cabaret card away from me.

Right after the arrest. I saw all of my salaries disappearing, you know. Where else could I make the money that I had been making money other than in New York? Nowhere. So I said, well, what is there left, you know? All I can play is off nights and three nights at the most in a nightclub and theaters. And fellows would come to me and say, "Hey, John, we want you to go into Birdland with us." I'd say, "I'm sorry, I can't take the job." So I'd have to recommend someone.

And after the recommendation do you think they were thankful? No. They didn't -- no-one even said thanks, have a drink, or here's five dollars, go and clean yourself up, or anything, you know. So I even stopped giving referrals, you know. Find them yourself, man. It's not my job, you know.
